description:
FILED s536c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) while building #1611's guard rows.  PRE-EXISTING (c950ad43 = main at s536; the same on 0affbe86).

`Pl/PExpr/Config.pm`'s `known_no_of_params` holds `cwd => 0` and `getcwd => 0`.  Neither is a perl keyword (`prototype("CORE::cwd")` dies) -- they are Cwd's functions, a module fact in the core table (CLAUDE.md rule 9a's smell).  The arity table decides the PARSE, so a list-operator spelling of a sub named `cwd` is split as `cwd() , 1, 2` and the statement falls through PExpr and is DROPPED:

    use Cwd; print((cwd 1, 2) =~ m{/} ? "ok\n" : "no\n");
      perl 5.40.3: ok
      PCL:  PCL: statement dropped at ... line 1: ... -- Bug. Fell through. Missing case: [... funcall ..., 'Token::Number<1>']

    BEGIN { *{"main::cwd"} = sub { "g-cwd(@_)" } } print cwd 1, 2;
      perl: g-cwd(1 2)        PCL: the same drop

Real Cwd's `cwd` takes no arguments, so the spelling is rare in practice; the zero-arity entry's PURPOSE is `cwd . "/x"` / `cwd eq $d` parsing as a term, which must keep working.  FIX SHAPE (not built): the arity is Cwd's fact -- `lib/Cwd.pm` declares `sub cwd ()` / `sub getcwd ()` (an empty prototype is a parse fact that crosses a `use`, #365's mechanism), and the two Config rows go; then a run-time glob install (no prototype) is a list operator as in perl.  Probe the term shapes (`cwd . "/x"`, `cwd eq $d`, `my @p = (cwd, 1)`) before and after.  #1611 (s536c) is the call-site NAMING half of the same family and did not touch the parse.

=== DONE (s536g) ===
Probed perl's Cwd first: `prototype(\&Cwd::cwd)` / getcwd / fastcwd / abs_path are all UNDEF -- no prototype, so no `()` declaration either.  The two `known_no_of_params` rows (`cwd => 0`, `getcwd => 0`) are DELETED (rule 9a: a module fact in the core table), and `Cwd` leaves `Pl::Parser::_extract_module_prototypes`' module-name skip list (the File::Spec / POSIX lesson: sub EXISTENCE is a parse fact), so `use Cwd`'s exports from lib/Cwd.pm make them known list operators.  perl = tree: `cwd . "/x"`, `cwd eq $d`, `(cwd, 1)`, `getcwd eq $d` stay zero-argument terms; `(cwd 1, 2)`, `BEGIN { *{"main::cwd"} = sub {...} } print cwd 1, 2`, a user `sub getcwd` with `getcwd 4, 5` take their arguments (was a DROP).  Without `use Cwd` a bare `cwd` is now perl's bareword.  Guard Pl/t/runtime-name-hygiene-01.t rows 16-17 (both fail on c8886b61).  Predicted over the 2,047-file list: every bare cwd/getcwd call head sits in a file that imports it (scratch pred-cwd.tsv), so no call changes.  Commit c4caf570.


=== CLOSED (s536 reviewing session, 2026-11-08 20:1x) === merged as MAIN-READY-83 f5ecb8fc (s536g, generation v2-13100). Review probes perl -> main 8f046c7a -> tree (scratchpad p536g/a b b2 c d.pl, 37 lines): tree = perl on every line; main died on -K 1 (`&main::(p-- ...)`), dropped `(cwd 1, 2)` and the three dynamic-method chains, and called the builtins for user subs say / fc / isa. Rows keyed on this task: none left (comp/parser.t 45, op/lc.t 7 and YAML-PP 54.glob.t left their baselines in the batch).
subject: `cwd LIST` / `getcwd LIST` (a list-operator call of a glob-installed or imported cwd) DROPS the statement: PExpr's arity table carries the Cwd functions `cwd => 0` / `getcwd => 0` as if they were perl builtins
